claims.sentence: The MHRA's August 2026 Safety Roundup advises more frequent liver function tests for people who recently had immunotherapy before starting sotorasib (Lumykras).
claims.evidence: Roundup item 'Increased liver monitoring for sotorasib (Lumykras) patients with recent immunotherapy'; advice is to healthcare professionals.

claims.sentence: The MHRA's August 2026 Safety Roundup says the sotorasib (Lumykras) product information has been updated.
claims.evidence: Roundup: 'following an update to the sotorasib Summary of Product Characteristics'.

claims.sentence: The MHRA advises more frequent liver function testing for patients who had immunotherapy recently before starting sotorasib.
A review of clinical data found a higher rate of liver injury in this group.
claims.evidence: Roundup: review of clinical data showed higher incidence of hepatotoxicity in this group.

claims.sentence: Recent immunotherapy may also be a risk factor for interstitial lung disease.
claims.evidence: Roundup: recent immunotherapy before sotorasib 'may also be a risk factor for interstitial lung disease (ILD)'.

claims.sentence: The MHRA says that, following an update to the summary of product characteristics for sotorasib (Lumykras), healthcare professionals should carry out more frequent liver function testing in patients who received immunotherapy recently, within the previous three months, before starting sotorasib.
claims.evidence: Roundup: HCPs should conduct more frequent liver function testing in patients who received immunotherapy within the previous 3 months before starting sotorasib. No schedule or cut-off beyond the 3 months is given or used.

claims.sentence: The Safety Roundup was published on 25 August 2026.
claims.evidence: Search text: August 2026 roundup on GOV.UK issued 25 August 2026.

claims.sentence: The MHRA cites a review of clinical data that found a higher rate of liver injury (hepatotoxicity) in this group than in patients who started sotorasib more than three months after their last immunotherapy dose or who never had immunotherapy.
claims.evidence: Roundup: higher incidence than in patients who started sotorasib more than 3 months after last immunotherapy dose or never had immunotherapy.

claims.sentence: It adds that recent immunotherapy before sotorasib may also be a risk factor for interstitial lung disease, a group of conditions that cause scarring and inflammation in the lungs.
claims.evidence: ILD risk-factor point supported. The 'group of conditions that cause scarring and inflammation' gloss is not in the roundup text; it is general medical background (textbook) and acceptable.

claims.sentence: The MHRA says sotorasib should be withheld in patients with severe liver injury, or if interstitial lung disease is suspected, and points clinicians to the summary of product characteristics for monitoring details.
claims.evidence: Roundup: withhold in severe hepatotoxicity or if ILD suspected; refers to SmPC for monitoring recommendations and dose modifications. Clinician-directed.

claims.sentence: The site's lung cancer page gives background.
claims.evidence: Internal pointer. The roundup PDF (assets.publishing.service.gov.uk) states sotorasib is indicated for KRAS G12C-mutated non-small cell lung cancer, so the link is now justified; the brief never states the indication itself.

dateEvidence: Search text for the gov.uk August 2026 roundup states it was issued 25 August 2026; consistent with the PDF listing. Not read on-page.
notes: 'Within 3 months' wording confirmed. The lung cancer link is now supported by the roundup PDF text (sotorasib indicated for KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC), so the brief need not be dropped; optionally add: 'Sotorasib is a medicine for KRAS G12C-mutated non-small cell lung cancer.' (supported by the PDF; the PDF text was fragmentary). A separate cohort study mentions a 6-week interval; irrelevant to the brief, do not add. No instructions to individuals, no 'safe' claims, no doses.
